overall_summary: Bitcoin faces mild pressure from ETF outflows but is overshadowed by stronger bullish catalysts today. Positive Fed signals, BlackRock's new income ETF launch, and easing geopolitical tensions from the US-Iran deal are lifting risk sentiment. Overall, the tone for crypto feels constructive with improving macro and institutional backdrops.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post $64M Net Outflow Monday Led by GBTC
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a net $64 million outflow on Monday, almost entirely from Grayscale's GBTC which lost $124 million. Other crypto ETFs for ether, XRP, Solana and more saw inflows. Traders should watch these flows closely as they directly influence spot Bitcoin buying or selling pressure from institutions.
items.impact: Continued mild selling pressure on Bitcoin price.

items.title: Bitcoin June Downturn Leaves $8.6 Billion Options Out of the Money
items.summary: With Bitcoin down about 12 percent this month, only 20 percent of options expiring June 26 are currently in the money. This leaves a large chunk of bullish positions underwater. Traders should note this could lead to reduced leverage or forced adjustments heading into expiry.
items.impact: Potential for volatility around options expiry but limited immediate price impact.

items.title: Fed Meeting Offers Three Signals That Could Boost Bitcoin
items.summary: Markets are focusing on the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and Chair Kevin Warsh's comments today. Analysts highlight potential dovish signals around policy that could support risk assets including Bitcoin. Traders should listen for any hints on rate cuts or liquidity that might reverse recent weakness.
items.impact: Possible positive catalyst for Bitcoin if signals are favorable.

items.title: BlackRock Launches Bitcoin Income ETF Targeting High Yields
items.summary: BlackRock introduced a new Bitcoin ETF using a covered call strategy aimed at generating yields in the high teens. This adds an income-focused product to the Bitcoin ETF lineup. Traders may see this as expanding institutional access and appeal for Bitcoin exposure.
items.impact: Could attract new capital into Bitcoin-related products over time.

items.title: Congress Reaches Deal on Housing Bill Banning CBDC Through 2030
items.summary: The Senate and House agreed on legislation that would ban central bank digital currencies in the US through 2030. This removes a potential competitor to decentralized assets like Bitcoin. Traders should view this as a regulatory win that supports Bitcoin's narrative as sound money.
items.impact: Positive long-term sentiment boost for Bitcoin.

items.title: US Retail Sales Beat Forecasts with 0.9% MoM Gain in May
items.summary: Retail sales jumped 0.9 percent month-over-month in May, well above the 0.5 percent consensus, with a strong 6.9 percent year-over-year rise. Consumer spending remains resilient despite higher energy costs and mixed sentiment readings. Traders should note this supports a soft-landing narrative but could keep the Fed cautious on inflation.
items.impact: Supports risk assets and growth outlook short-term.

items.title: Fed Set to Hold Rates Steady at First Warsh-Led FOMC Meeting
items.summary: Markets price in near-certainty of no change to the federal funds rate target range at today's 2pm ET decision, expected to stay at 3.50-3.75 percent. New Chair Kevin Warsh's first meeting focuses on communications and data dependence amid sticky inflation. Any hawkish tilt in the statement or projections could pressure risk assets.
items.impact: Hold likely limits immediate volatility but sets tone for future policy.

items.title: Pending Home Sales and Business Inventories Also Due Today
items.summary: May pending home sales and April business inventories releases are scheduled alongside retail sales. These will provide additional color on housing and supply chain health. Weak housing data could offset strong retail numbers for a mixed macro picture.
items.impact: Adds to data-heavy session but secondary to retail and Fed.

items.title: US and Iran reach framework deal to end war
items.summary: The United States and Iran have agreed on a preliminary deal that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, and halting fighting. The memorandum of understanding is expected to be signed in Geneva on Friday. Traders should watch this closely because reduced geopolitical risk in the Middle East typically supports risk assets like Bitcoin by easing energy market tensions and lowering safe-haven demand.
items.impact: Eases oil supply concerns and supports broader risk appetite.

items.title: Oil prices slide on Iran deal and Hormuz reopening hopes
items.summary: Brent crude has dropped to its lowest level since early March as hopes grow for a quick signing of the US-Iran framework agreement. The deal is expected to allow Iran to resume oil exports and fully reopen the critical Strait of Hormuz chokepoint. Crypto traders care because lower oil prices reduce inflation pressures and often correlate with stronger flows into risk assets.
items.impact: Lower energy costs support equities and crypto sentiment.

items.title: G7 leaders back Trump's Iran deal at summit
items.summary: Group of Seven leaders praised the emerging US-Iran agreement as a breakthrough during their meeting in France. President Trump highlighted progress while noting the deal is not entirely final and could see adjustments. Markets are reacting positively to the diplomatic momentum, which reduces the chance of further military escalation in a key energy region.
items.impact: Signals coordinated international support for de-escalation.
